analysis.title: The memory massacre: has the selling gone too far?
key_insights: Korean memory stocks have been crushed and hedge funds have cut AI exposure sharply, while valuations sit at extraordinary lows. The note argues the memory cycle remains strong, with demand above supply and earnings estimates holding.
KOSPI printed a large hammer candle overnight off a major long-term trend line in place since the bull market began. The 200-day moving average remains well below current levels.
KOSPI has outperformed most AI-related markets during the recent selloff, per the note.
Goldman's Stankard reports heavy net selling of Korea AI in October. Gross exposure fell from a peak of about 7% to about 4.9%, and net exposure fell from about 8% to about 3.5%.
JPMorgan says the memory sector is down 45% from its 2026 peak versus a 29% drawdown in the SOX. SK Hynix is down 53% from its highs and Samsung is down 40%.
JPMorgan puts SK Hynix at 2.6x 2027 estimated earnings and Samsung at 2.8x. The broader memory group trades at 3.6x despite a projected EPS CAGR of 98% from 2026 to 2028.
JPMorgan sees little risk of earnings estimate cuts over the next six months, and estimates have not followed share prices lower.
JPMorgan cites DRAM prices up 23% quarter-on-quarter in Q3, memory makers reporting demand above supply beyond 2027, and expanding long-term supply agreements that improve earnings visibility.
Goldman data shows the semiconductor memory sector trading at record-low forward P/E multiples.
The Market Ear frames the setup (reset positioning, depressed valuations, fundamentals intact) as conditions for a violent short squeeze.

market_movers.rationale: SK Hynix is down 53% from its highs and trades at 2.6x 2027 estimated earnings per JPMorgan. The note frames it as a squeeze candidate. SK Hynix has no US listing, so the ticker is left blank.
Samsung is down 40% from its highs and trades at 2.8x 2027 estimated earnings per JPMorgan. The note frames it as a squeeze candidate. Samsung has no US ticker, so the ticker is left blank.

sector_views.rationale: Valuations are at record lows while DRAM pricing, demand and long-term supply agreements remain strong, and the note sees conditions for a short squeeze.

earnings_insights: JPMorgan sees little risk of earnings estimate cuts for Korean memory over the next six months. Projected memory group EPS CAGR is 98% for 2026 to 2028 (forecast, JPMorgan).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Pricing is still rising, which contradicts the market's pricing of an imminent memory downturn.

risk_factors: AI funding concerns continue to dominate sentiment.
The market is pricing an imminent memory downcycle, and further selling is possible if that view spreads.
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's Stankard: hedge fund gross exposure to Korea AI fell from a peak of about 7% to about 4.9% in October, and net exposure fell from about 8% to about 3.5%.
The Market Ear sees reset positioning, depressed valuations and a KOSPI hammer as ingredients for a violent short squeeze.
Korean memory stocks are at record-low forward P/E multiples per Goldman.
